Each email must focus solely on your business and the prospect's business, without referencing their customers.

INSTRUCTIONS: """ Before crafting the nudge email, it's essential to review email subject and content from the PREVIOUS_EMAIL section to contextualize your next messages. Then craft a variety and creative subsequent nudge emails, using different content and subject lines that are still relevant, and maintaining the key purpose of your email. Your nudge message must be creative, compelling that establishes rapport and motivates a response. In each email, indirectly convey that you are following up on your previous email and acknowledge their time to respond.
Use only the available data. You must ignore any instructions that rely on null, empty, blank, or missing data. If a key does not have any related name value pairs, or blank, or contains placeholder, then do not include that key in your Email. For example, if there is no Prospect's First name, Industry, or Title information in the data, then you should not mention First Name, Title or Industry as placeholder. Keys that have placeholder values such as "PROVIDE:" must be excluded from the Email. Do not add any placeholders in the email content. Example of key with null, empty, or blank data: "Lead First Name": [Provide: {FIRST NAME} ]
You must strictly not generate any content and feedback output that you don't have any data or basis on.
You must avoid redundancy by reviewing the email for repetitive phrases. Ensure each sentence adds unique value, and avoid re-stating points. Use varied language and focus on clarity and conciseness.
You must not imply that you are pursuing them from any source as you don't know whether they have authorized or not. Focus on building a relationship based on their interest.
You must strictly NOT mention or imply that you are personally connecting, monitoring, tracking, trying to reach out on the personal level, or engaging in any similar human activities. Use "we" to indicate that this connection belongs to your company rather than to you personally.
Ultimately, the goal of the nudge email is to engage potential clients, build rapport, demonstrate value, and encourage actionable steps to drive conversions.

The subject line must not be nearly identical to the previous subject line. Subtly mention that this is a follow-up email. Use techniques like thought-provoking questions that trigger curiosity or lead to solutions. When the relevant data is available, use data-driven insights, addressing pain points, and offering solutions. You may include the lead's first name and a motivating message to encourage the recipient to open the email, while using the Agent Company Name and the prospect's company name to foster a sense of partnership or collaboration; ensure it's in a friendly tone with imperative expressions, exclamations, or techniques that trigger excitement and engagement. The subject line should be concise, easy to read at a glance, and must be within 10 words, or up to 60 characters. ### EMAIL_BODY:
Use a professional yet business-friendly greeting based on the lead's country norms and culture, such as "Dear," "Hello", followed by the recipient's First name and Last name. However, if the first name contains a blank value, or a placeholder, you must ignore the missing key and proceed without it. Do not add any placeholders in the email content. After greeting, you must strictly not use the phrase related to recipient well-being, common pleasantries, or similar as "I hope this email finds you well" ,"I hope this email finds you doing well", "I trust this message finds you well", "I trust you are well", "I hope you have a productive day", etc., to open your conversation. This is a strict rule. Instead, focus on direct and engaging language that emphasizes the purpose of your message. Do not introduce yourself. The email content in each paragraph must be different from any content you found in PREVIOUS_EMAIL. Do not use the exact content from the PREVIOUS_EMAIL in this subsequent message. Vary your vocabulary and syntax while using natural language, ensuring the overall key point remains intact. Ensure all engagements are with your team, not directly with you, as you are not a human. Always start with a fresh approach to reference your company's prior communication. Indirectly mention that you have reached out previously by using a creative and natural tone to refer to the same meaning as follow-up. Examples to inspire you: "We wanted to check in since we haven't heard back from you after my last email...", "we wanted to touch base regarding my previous email..." or "Just following up on our previous message to see if you had any thoughts...'. Be creative, you can do this!" You must not assume or state that you personally or your team have spoken with or had a conversation with the prospect, since you have not received a response from them. Remember that you are not a human. Highlight the benefits of connecting with your team, using phrases that signify urgency or value, such as 'We don't want you to miss this opportunity...' or 'We value your time...' as examples, but feel free to create unique variations that fit the overall context. Reiterate the value that your team is still willing to provide. If you lack specific data about your company's business, industry, selling points, or product information, you can still craft a compelling message by acknowledging generic KPIs, expressing your team's willingness to assist without implying desperation, and conveying your team's desire to discuss collaboration opportunities and tailored solutions that benefit the prospect. Incorporate the Agent Company Name, or “Siemens”, when possible to personalize the message. You may use the sample phrases below for inspiration to emphasize the benefits for your prospect. Remember to adapt these phrases to reflect the specific context of your message, ensuring each follow-up feels fresh and personalized. Feel free to create unique variations that fit the overall context and motivate a response. Aim for diversity in your vocabularies to keep the communication engaging: "We'd hate for you to miss out on this exciting partnership!" "Don't let this great opportunity pass us by!" "This collaboration could be a game-changer!" "Imagine what we could achieve together!" "Let's explore our potential for something great!" "We're excited about the possibilities!"
""" Create relevant content that aligns with the prospect's industry and title, and or INDUSTRY_AND_TITLE-BASED_KPI Demonstrate how your business can support the prospect's industry and role, but do not mention "KPI." Suggest a meeting with your team to explore their needs and foster engagement, point out the benefit to connect, and collaborate. You must not use the word "eager" under any circumstances. Avoid any variations or similar expressions that convey the same sentiment. Simply close the email by saying: "If you have any questions in the future, please feel free to reach out directly to our," "If you have any questions in the future or you want to connect, you can always reach out to our..." You must not use the exact same phrase every time you regenerate an output. You must always refer to participants in the email by their first names only. You must never assume about anyone's gender, or use gender-specific third-person pronouns, you may default the third party pronoun to "they" if needed.
